newsitem.title: UK: BAA windfall tax regret, says not main target.
newsitem.headline: BAA windfall tax regret, says not main target.

text.p: UK airport operator BAA Plc said in a statement on Wednesday that it regretted being targeted for a windfall tax by the Labour government.

But the group added that the size of its levy reflected its own view that it should not be made a primary target. BAA did not quantify the size of its exposure to the tax, which has not been broken down company-by-company in the budget's accompanying Inland Revenue notes.

Sir John Egan, chief executive of BAA, said in a statement he regretted the group's inclusion in the list of windfall taxable companies but added it was pleasing that the group had not been made a main target for the tax.
"We have maintained throughout that BAA should not be a primary target for the windfall tax, although we understood we could be included for legal reasons," said Egan.
BAA was named in a list of privatised utility companies liable for the tax after the Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown completed his first budget speech earlier on Wednesday.
The tax has been levied against companies privatised by flotation and subject to economic regulation.
UK analysts agreed from initial calculations that BAA would be hit fairly lightly in comparison with other companies.
